title: Contextual priority-shift shedder with graceful fidelity tiers
creator: Ariana Kim
description: Goal: Implement a contextual priority-shift load shedder that adjusts admission and fidelity tiers per-request during regional congestion and multi-region failover. The shedder should integrate with circuit breakers, SLO targets, and tenant fairness heuristics so we maintain critical SLAs while minimizing customer-visible regressions. Background: Current admission logic uses static token-bucket thresholds and coarse priority lanes. During regional pressure we observed broad full-fidelity drops causing high error churn for mid-tier customers. This ticket designs a runtime component that: 1) computes a per-request criticality score (SLO urgency + customer tier + recent error budget usage + inferred latency sensitivity), 2) uses that score to apply a contextual priority shift that can push requests between fidelity tiers (full model, quantized short-path, partial response stub), and 3) coordinates with region-level circuit breakers to progressively tighten admission and enable soft fallbacks. Key components: - Admission controller plugin to compute criticality score and annotate requests with target fidelity tier. - Priority queue subsystem that supports time-decayed weights and deterministic tie-breaking to avoid starvation. - Graceful fidelity tiers: full, trimmed, stubbed, and delayed-execution (deferred queue). - Circuit breaker integration: open thresholds trigger immediate aggressive trimming; half-open probes allow sample traffic to verify recovery. - Metrics and telemetry: per-tenant SLO burn rate, per-tier latency P50/P95/P99, eviction rates, fairness delta, and regional failover counters. Success criteria: - During simulated region surge, preserve P99 latency for P0 customers within configured SLOs 95% of the time while reducing overall token spend by >= 18%. - Fairness: no single tenant experiences >3x the eviction rate of its weight for more than 10 minutes. - Rollout: gradual canary with traffic shadowing and a safe rollback path. Design decisions & trade-offs: - Per-request scoring provides finer control than lane-only shedding but adds CPU cost; mitigated by caching scores for session tokens and sampling rate-limited computation. - Deterministic tie-break avoids flapping but complicates dynamic weight changes; we accept slight lag in weight updates (30s) for stability. - Deferred execution (delayed queue) increases tail work and operational complexity; we will cap deferred queue depth by tenant to bound resource usage. Rollout plan: 1) Build admission plugin + unit tests. 2) Local canary in one cluster region with 5% traffic, collect metrics and compare to baseline. 3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% with automated rollback on SLO regressions. 4) Enable multi-region coordination after single-region steady-state. Observability: dashboard templates in Console for per-tenant eviction rates, fidelity transitions, and per-region circuit breaker state. Runbook: documented progressive steps for operators to shift thresholds, blacklist tenants for emergency, and disable deferred queue. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is no-op (existing thresholds) until policy is explicitly enabled per-deployment. Open questions: - Exact formula weighting for recent error budget vs latency sensitivity (propose starting 60/40). - How aggressively to allow automatic tenant-weight decay versus operator overrides. - Policy authoring surface in Console UX (follow-up PM/Design ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Admission plugin computes and attaches a fidelity tier for each request and is exercised by unit tests
End-to-end benchmarks show CPU overhead <= 6% at target throughput for score computation (5K req/s cluster)
Canary run (5% traffic) demonstrates no P0 SLO regression over 24h under synthetic surge profile
Dashboards for per-tenant eviction and fidelity transitions created and linked in Console
Runbook with rollback steps and emergency tenant blacklist published
